hypotheses.justification: The type of the theorem, `posDetInt n ≤ (commensurator (SLnZ n)).toSubmonoid`, mentions only `n` (`SLnZ`, `intEntries`, `posDetInt`, `Matrix.GLPos`, `commensurator` are all defined for every `n : ℕ`, with no dimension hypothesis), so `[NeZero n]` is included only by the instance-implicit auto-inclusion rule; `omit [NeZero n] in` therefore removes it without changing the statement. The current proof uses it only through `mem_commensurator_of_hasIntEntries`, whose chain (`conj_mat_det_one`, using `Nat.sub_one_add_one_eq_of_pos (NeZero.pos n)`) really needs `n ≠ 0`; but the missing case `n = 0` is trivial. At `n = 0` the carrier is `GL (Fin 0) ℚ = (Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) ℚ)ˣ`, and `Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) ℚ` is a subsingleton (`Matrix.subsingleton_of_empty_left` for `IsEmpty (Fin 0)`), so `GL (Fin 0) ℚ` is a subsingleton (units equal by `Units.ext` and `Subsingleton.elim`), hence every `g` satisfies `g = 1`. Since `commensurator (SLnZ 0)` is a subgroup it contains `1`, so every element of `posDetInt 0` lies in `(commensurator (SLnZ 0)).toSubmonoid` (this is just `Subgroup.one_mem` transported along `g = 1`, and is exactly `Commensurable.refl` for the unique element). A proof without the hypothesis is a case split: if `n = 0`, rewrite `g` to `1` using the subsingleton instance and use `one_mem`; if `n > 0`, obtain `haveI : NeZero n := ⟨Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp h⟩` locally and apply the existing proof through `mem_commensurator_of_hasIntEntries`. (This only deletes `[NeZero n]` from this theorem; `n` itself is needed since it occurs in the statement.)
